status.grok: TESTED 2026-06-09. CHAT DETECTION OK — driven by the network interceptor (/rest/app-chat/conversations), NOT the DOM. The DOM item selector 'a[href*="/c/"]' now matches 0 (Grok moved sidebar history to shadcn buttons with no /c/ href), but this is harmless — detection works via network, and the selector stays as a fallback. Input 'textarea' OK. IDENTITY FIXED — old regex '"userId":"<uuid>"' required literal quotes, but Grok now streams it escaped in an RSC payload (raw text: ...\"userId\":\"13ab1054-...\",\"email\":\"...). New regexPattern 'userId[^a-f0-9]{1,12}(<uuid>)' matches userId followed by 1-12 non-hex chars (the escaped ":" gap) then the uuid — escape-depth agnostic, also works if Grok reverts to unescaped quotes. Verified the uuid sits immediately before the account email. DOM SCRAPING — INVESTIGATED, CONFIRMED INFEASIBLE (do not chase). Grok history is behind an on-demand 'History' button that opens a dialog; entries render as JS <button>s, not <a href>. Verified across 3 probes: full sidebar attribute dump found 0 elements carrying the chat id (no /c/ href, no data-id/data-href/uuid attribute); the History dialog list had 12 buttons and 0 anchors; the only /c/ anchor in the whole page is the CURRENT chat (page URL), never a history entry. Even if the id were in an attribute, the detector's automated scrapes never click 'History', so DOM detection would never fire. DECISION: Grok detection is network-interceptor-only by design (/rest/app-chat/conversations, see network-interceptor.ts). The DOM item selector 'a[href*="/c/"]' is kept ONLY as a dormant fallback in case Grok reverts to anchor-based history — it is expected to match 0 today and that is correct, not a bug.
status.claude: VERIFIED CURRENT + FIXED (2026-06-09) — container 'nav', item 'a[href^="/chat/"]' 6/6, idPattern 6/6, input '...ProseMirror', identity /api/account->uuid (200, ffffc040...) all matched. FIX APPLIED: title selector changed from 'span, div, p' (which matched the outer div and produced DOUBLED titles, e.g. 'Personal fitness tracking PWAPersonal fitness tracking PWA') to '.sr-only, .block.truncate'. Each Claude chat item renders the title twice: span.sr-only (a11y copy) + span.block.truncate (visible copy); the old selector's first tree-order match was the wrapper div whose textContent concatenated both. New selector targets a single-title node (neither matches the doubled wrapper: the outer span has 'truncate' but not 'block'). detector.ts still falls back to link.textContent if absent. Do NOT add bare 'span'/'div'/'.truncate' as fallbacks — they re-match the doubled wrapper.
